reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it documents an ordinary GameStop purchase and a personal Fortnite redemption demonstration involving a 1,000 V-Bucks code and displayed redemption flow. Requests for likes, comments, and an Epic Games username relate to channel engagement and a proposed in-game item giveaway, while obtaining additional codes is described as visiting GameStop locations rather than requesting payment or investment participation. The records do not establish deceptive behavior or an adverse outcome, though they do not verify whether the proposed giveaway occurred or whether every external claim was accurate.

Success your code has been successfully redeemed
it says fortnite 1000 vbucks the the promotion code has been accepted for one item
There it is guys the merry mint pickaxe unlockable screen

opening.argument: The video links a promised digital reward to immediate viewer actions, which is the operative structure of a low-barrier reward solicitation. Viewers are told to act within five seconds, like the video, and post an Epic Games username in exchange for an attempt to place the Minty pickaxe in their account. The speaker then extends the appeal by promising to obtain more codes for viewers. That is more than simply documenting a purchase: it conditions access to a game asset on engagement and personal-account information, while leaving the delivery dependent on the speaker's future actions.

citations.quote: drop a like in the next 5 seconds and comment down below your Epic Games username because Im gonna try and hook up you down in the comments below With this brand new mentee pickaxe in your locker account
so that is what i'm gonna do later i'm gonna go later afternoon to get more codes for you guys

rebuttal.rebuttal: The purchase and redemption quotes establish only that the speaker obtained and used one code for himself. They do not answer the separate promise made to viewers: liking, commenting with an Epic username, and waiting for the speaker to provide a pickaxe. A successful self-redemption therefore cannot validate the promised giveaway.

citations.quote: Success your code has been successfully redeemed
comment down below your Epic Games username because Im gonna try and hook up you down in the comments below

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The cited request says the speaker will “try” to provide the item, not that viewers must pay or that delivery is guaranteed. The evidence shows a real purchase and successful redemption for the speaker, while the record does not establish that any viewer was charged, supplied credentials, or suffered a loss. Engagement requests alone do not prove a deceptive reward scheme.

citations.quote: i just got home right now from gamStop I went and bought the brand new vbucks card
Success your code has been successfully redeemed

opening.argument: Several concrete risk signals appear together: a five-second deadline, a free game-asset appeal, external redemption steps, and exposed codes. The speaker also describes a one-per-person restriction and proposes visiting other GameStop locations to obtain more codes, framing a retail limit as something to work around. The redemption flow itself requires entering a PIN and confirming a platform- and region-specific 1,000 V-Bucks code. These details make the offer unusually easy to misunderstand and encourage urgency and code-focused participation, even though the video does not establish clear eligibility, allocation, or fulfillment terms for viewers.

citations.quote: drop a like in the next 5 seconds
the only way you guys can get more is by going to different gamestops near your location

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the code a normal retail item does not remove the risk signals surrounding the audience-facing offer. The video combines urgency and a promised game asset with instructions to comment an account identifier, then shows a scratched code and a confirmation flow. The defense establishes transaction mechanics, not that the solicitation was transparent or that viewers could safely receive the promised reward.

citations.quote: drop a like in the next 5 seconds and comment down below your Epic Games username

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The visual and audio evidence show an ordinary card redemption with explicit platform and regional conditions, not a hidden transfer of money or credentials. The one-per-person statement describes store availability, and the speaker's later plan concerns buying additional cards. Urgency and exposed codes may look unpolished, but they do not establish deception, an adverse outcome, or a false reward.

citations.quote: i just got home right now from gamStop I went and bought the brand new vbucks card
the promotion code has been redeemed as you guys can see

opening.argument: Although presented as a trip to GameStop and a redemption demonstration, the video functions primarily as promotion for participation. Its title centers an exclusive pickaxe and V-Bucks, the description solicits likes, subscriptions, and use of the creator's code, and the closing asks viewers to submit Epic usernames while promising attempts to obtain more codes. The store visit and successful personal redemption supply promotional credibility, but the audience-facing message steers viewers toward engagement and an uncertain reward rather than merely reporting an ordinary purchase.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the retail setting as dispositive, but a real store visit can also be the vehicle for promotion. The documented purchase does not negate the separate calls to use the creator's code, comment an Epic username, and expect more codes. Nor does a personal unlock screen establish that the audience-facing promise was fulfilled.

citations.quote: USE CODE “braniyt” IN ITEM SHOP
comment below your epic games user name I'm gonna try to go out later again to get to gamestop game more codes

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The title and description identify Fortnite merchandise and ordinary channel promotion, while the video demonstrates an actual purchase and redemption rather than directing viewers to invest or send money. A creator code and requests for likes or comments are common promotional engagement. The evidence does not show that viewers were required to buy anything, that the creator misrepresented the redeemed item, or that the proposed giveaway failed.
